From 1cba96c0a795124c3229293ed7b5b5765e66f259 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Koichiro Den <den@valinux.co.jp>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:38:56 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] PCI: endpoint: pci-ep-msi: Fix error unwind and prevent
 double alloc

pci_epf_alloc_doorbell() stores the allocated doorbell message array in
epf->db_msg/epf->num_db before requesting MSI vectors. If MSI allocation
fails, the array is freed but the EPF state may still point to freed
memory.

Clear epf->db_msg and epf->num_db on the MSI allocation failure path so
that later cleanup cannot double-free the array and callers can retry
allocation.

Also return -EBUSY when doorbells have already been allocated to prevent
leaking or overwriting an existing allocation.

Fixes: 1c3b002c6bf6 ("PCI: endpoint: Add RC-to-EP doorbell support using platform MSI controller")
Signed-off-by: Koichiro Den <den@valinux.co.jp>
Signed-off-by: Manivannan Sadhasivam <mani@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Frank Li <Frank.Li@nxp.com>
Reviewed-by: Niklas Cassel <cassel@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260217063856.3759713-4-den@valinux.co.jp

diff --git a/drivers/pci/endpoint/pci-ep-msi.c b/drivers/pci/endpoint/pci-ep-msi.c
index 51c19942a81e..1395919571f8 100644
--- a/drivers/pci/endpoint/pci-ep-msi.c
+++ b/drivers/pci/endpoint/pci-ep-msi.c
@@ -50,6 +50,9 @@ int pci_epf_alloc_doorbell(struct pci_epf *epf, u16 num_db)
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 
+	if (epf->db_msg)
+		return -EBUSY;
+
 	domain = of_msi_map_get_device_domain(epc->dev.parent, 0,
 					      DOMAIN_BUS_PLATFORM_MSI);
 	if (!domain) {
@@ -79,6 +82,8 @@ int pci_epf_alloc_doorbell(struct pci_epf *epf, u16 num_db)
 	if (ret) {
 		dev_err(dev, "Failed to allocate MSI\n");
 		kfree(msg);
+		epf->db_msg = NULL;
+		epf->num_db = 0;
 		return ret;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

**File:** `drivers/pci/endpoint/pci-ep-msi.c`

- **Prevent double allocation:** Added an early check at the beginning of `pci_epf_alloc_doorbell()` that returns `-EBUSY` if `epf->db_msg` is already non-NULL. This prevents overwriting an existing doorbell allocation or leaking memory on repeated calls.

- **Fix error unwind on MSI allocation failure:** In the failure path after `pci_irq_get_vector()` or `platform_msi_domain_alloc_irqs()` fails, the allocated doorbell message array (`msg`) is freed, but the corresponding EPF fields (`epf->db_msg` and `epf->num_db`) were left set to the old (now freed) values. The patch clears these fields (`epf->db_msg = NULL`, `epf->num_db = 0`) before returning the error, ensuring the EPF state remains consistent and preventing potential double-free or use-after-free in subsequent cleanup or retry attempts.

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both changes reside in the same function (`pci_epf_alloc_doorbell()`) and together enforce correct resource life-cycle management:

- The first change prevents **re‑entry** into the allocation logic when doorbells are already configured, avoiding resource leaks.
- The second change ensures that on **allocation failure**, the EPF state fully reflects the failure, so any later attempt to clean up or retry will not operate on stale pointers.

The combination guarantees that the function either successfully allocates doorbells and updates `epf` fields, or leaves the `epf` state unmodified (or cleanly cleared) in every error path.
